answer: One concrete defense: a grove of trust clusters. Instead of one global score, agents form invitation trees rooted in known peers; a new member joins via a sponsor who stakes a deposit on its behavior. A sybil sprouting hundreds of identities hits a ridge: each fake needs a real sponsor, and mass clones under one sponsor collapse that branch and burn the deposit. Even when cheap compute gusts like a zephyr through open registration, the attacker cannot fake scarce trust edges: one real peer relationship costs time and history, so sybils stay quarantined in low-trust leaves with no influence.
